history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V11 workload, mode, jobs, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability, acceptance, allocation, and GC-pause decision. It versions the fresh-process CPU and resident-memory attribution contract and removes only those implemented metrics from the pending inventory; any later workload, boundary, jobs, checksum, metric, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Adds phase-boundary getrusage process user/system CPU and peak RSS plus the live Mach resident-size gauge. CPU is delta-attributed to configuration, warmup, and invocation; peak and retained RSS remain exact boundary gauges. Invocation retained RSS is sampled after the workload host checkpoint and before Context destruction. Scored timing rows remain uninstrumented.

tier_attribution.scope: one fresh zig-js process and context per workload and structural variant; Context backing profiling and process-resource boundaries begin before arena/Context construction
tier_attribution.invocation: one inherited full-work call with the frozen jobs and lane-zero input; retained RSS is sampled after its host checkpoint and before Context destruction
tier_attribution.equivalence: For warmup and invocation independently, each base/variant pair must select the same non-empty set of tree-walker, VM, baseline, optimizer, optimizer-OSR, and deoptimization paths and allocate exactly the same number of environments. Exact tier, runtime, synchronization, allocation, GC-pause, process CPU, resident-memory, and worker values remain visible rather than normalized away; every Wasm workload must record an invocation-phase Wasm dispatch.
tier_attribution.timing_isolation: Attribution uses fresh opt-in processes and contexts outside every scored timing row; normal contexts retain the original allocator chain, disabled contention counters, null execution-attribution pointer, no GC-pause sample storage, and no process-resource queries.

recognizer_audit.prohibited: Every representative workload identifier is absent from engine source. Identifiers exist only in the owned workload, manifest, and benchmark tooling.
